SVP, Product Management – Data Products & Strategy

Location:
Canada – Remote or Mississauga, ON – Hybrid

Travel to Office expectations**

For Remote Roles

For Hybrid Roles
: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.

At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare.

With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work.

At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.

Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.

Position Summary

Reporting directly to the Chief Product & Technology Officer (CPTO), the Senior Vice President, Product Management – Data Products & Strategy establishes and leads PointClickCare’s enterprise strategy for Data as a Product. This executive leader is accountable for transforming PointClickCare’s unique data assets, ecosystem position, and network scale into differentiated products, strategic growth opportunities, and new sources of enterprise value.

The role owns the long-term strategy for customer-facing data products, APIs, interoperability, marketplace capabilities, data monetization, and data-enabled AI solutions while ensuring appropriate protection of intellectual property, privacy, and regulatory compliance. As a member of the senior Product Leadership Team, the SVP influences corporate strategy, investment priorities, ecosystem partnerships, and growth initiatives while leading a team of senior Product leaders responsible for PointClickCare’s data product portfolio.

Key Responsibilities

Define and lead PointClickCare’s enterprise Data Products strategy, including establishing a multi-year vision for Data as a Product that aligns with corporate objectives, growth priorities, and evolving market opportunities.
Identify, evaluate, and champion new business models and growth opportunities enabled by PointClickCare’s data assets, network scale, interoperability capabilities, and ecosystem partnerships.
Serve as the executive sponsor for customer-facing data strategy and ensure alignment across Product, Engineering, AI, Corporate Strategy, Legal, Go-to-Market, and the Corporate Data Office.
Own the strategy, roadmap, performance, and long-term success of PointClickCare’s data products portfolio, including customer-facing data products, APIs, interoperability services, marketplace capabilities, and AI-enabled solutions.
Establish investment priorities, resource allocation decisions, portfolio success measures, and business outcomes that balance customer value, market opportunity, and financial performance.
Drive adoption, customer value realization, commercial performance, and scalable product growth through strong portfolio management and strategic execution.
Lead PointClickCare’s enterprise strategy for data monetization, marketplace growth, and ecosystem expansion.
Define customer access models, API strategies, pricing frameworks, packaging approaches, and commercial models that support sustainable growth while preserving trust and protecting intellectual property.
Identify new revenue opportunities, strategic partnerships, and ecosystem capabilities that strengthen PointClickCare’s competitive position and expand customer value.
Represent PointClickCare’s data strategy with executive stakeholders, customers, strategic partners, industry analysts, and industry organizations.
Lead executive-level discussions related to data products, healthcare interoperability, marketplace participation, data monetization, and AI-enabled customer solutions.
Build relationships that influence product direction, market positioning, and long-term growth opportunities across the healthcare technology landscape.
Lead, develop, and scale a high-performing product leadership organization through senior leaders, including VPs and Directors.
Establish succession planning, leadership development, talent strategies, and organizational capabilities that strengthen expertise in data products, APIs, ecosystem platforms, marketplace solutions, and monetization strategies.
Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, customer focus, and execution excellence.

Required Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, Healthcare Informatics, Information Systems, or a related field.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in product management, technology, data products, platform strategy, enterprise software, or related disciplines.
Demonstrated success defining and executing enterprise-level product, growth, or business strategies with measurable impact on organizational performance, customer outcomes, and financial results.
Proven experience leading large, complex product or technology organizations through multiple layers of leadership, including developing senior leaders and building organizational capability.
Track record of leading enterprise transformation initiatives requiring alignment across multiple functions, competing priorities, and significant organizational change.
Deep expertise in data products, APIs, interoperability, marketplace and ecosystem strategies, data monetization models, AI-enabled products, and the business dynamics of data-driven organizations.
Strong strategic, financial, and operational acumen, including ownership of portfolio-level investment decisions, business cases, risk management, and performance outcomes.
Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders, shape investment decisions, and represent organizational strategy with customers, partners, analysts, and other external stakeholders.
Experience leading marketplace, ecosystem, platform, or data monetization strategies is highly preferred.
Experience within healthcare technology, post-acute care, payer, provider, or other highly regulated industries is preferred.
Experience engaging with industry analysts, strategic partners, customer advisory groups, or external industry bodies is preferred.
Ability to balance growth objectives, customer needs, regulatory requirements, and intellectual property protection in a complex business environment.

jobs.description:
Venture outside the ordinary - TMX Careers

The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets. United as a global team, we’re connecting cross-functionally, traversing industries and geographies, moving opportunity into action, advancing global economic growth, and propelling progress. Through a rich exchange of ideas, meaningful collaboration, and a nimble operating model, we're powering some of the nation's most critical systems, fueling capital formation and innovation, bringing increased opportunity to business visionaries, product ingenuity to consumers, and career exploration to our team.

Ready to be part of the action?

Reporting to the President, CDCC, this role is a critical strategic resource focused on accelerating Post Trade's strategy and objectives. The Managing Director will drive the execution of complex, high-impact market modernization initiatives, providing dedicated delivery leadership to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC.

The main function of this role is to provide dedicated support to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC in delivering the Post Trade product and client centric solutions. Success hinges on a proven capital markets expert with deep knowledge of the Canadian capital markets, with an emphasis on fixed income, derivatives and repo markets knowledge, established relationships with key industry stakeholders. This expertise is vital in driving strategic development and managing complex alignment across TMX and core industry partners, including the Bank of Canada (BoC) and CIMPA participants, optimizing and aligning the Post Trade delivery strategy, with special initial focus on delivering and establishing the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and Repo 2.0.

Reports To: President, CDCC and Co-Head, Post-Trade Services
Job Location: This role is hybrid (2-3 days/week in the office) - we are open to candidates being located in one of our Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal.

Key Responsibilities

Program Delivery, Stakeholder Coordination, and Optimization
Unified Product-to-Delivery Lifecycle: Partner deeply with the Product Teams across Post Trade to translate product visions, commercial goals, and market requirements into robust, executable program delivery roadmaps.
Cross-Functional Delivery Governance: Establish rigorous execution frameworks, milestones, and governance models that ensure Post-Trade Innovations, CDCC, and CDS operate in perfect lockstep.
Strategy and Delivery Support: Provide dedicated, strategic and delivery support to Post Trade Innovations, CDCC and CDS to ensure the efficient execution of the overarching Post Trade delivery strategy.
Strategic Initiative Leadership: Provide strategic support for the execution and alignment of major market modernization initiatives, specifically the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and the Repo program.
Central Bank Coordination: Serve as the primary liaison to ensure strategic and operational alignment required for the Bank of Canada's (BoC) integration into the Post Trade framework, including the implementation of the CCP tri-party repo platform.
Market and Client Engagement: Help cultivate and maintain relationships with key stakeholders (e.g., BoC, CIMPA) to gather strategic insights, champion clearing initiatives, and validate new service proposals for Post Trade.
Internal Alignment: Ensure optimal, formalized deliveries with key internal stakeholders to efficiently advance CCMS, Repo 2.0, and other core business objectives.

Governance & Execution Frameworks
Enforce key governance, including the formal escalation path and milestone criteria.
Take direct responsibility for strategic and operational conflict resolution across CDS and CDCC business lines.

Execution & Representation
Serve as the primary coordinator for external representation with Clearstream.
Establish a strict pre-briefing protocol for client engagements to ensure unified messaging regarding value propositions.
Design and implement a mandatory, structured knowledge-transfer and cross-training program to decentralize business and product expertise.

Operational Accountability & Resource Management
Enforce mandatory participation of all dedicated resources in CCMS squad meetings and planning sessions.
Implement unified resource-tracking dashboards for visibility into team capacity and competing priorities.
Provide formal performance evaluation input to the functional leaders of dedicated resources.
Maintain authority to initiate external recruiting processes if internal resource constraints delay critical strategic deliverables.

Leadership and Guidance
Manage hiring, training and development of team members; set comprehensive objectives for individual and organizational performance and growth, enforcing accountability at all levels.
Recruit, mentor, and elevate a world-class team of delivery professionals and subject matter experts. Instill a culture of extreme ownership, high psychological safety, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate with other senior resources to ensure that objectives are aligned across all functions and business units, and create a culture of change and continuous improvement.
Challenge the status quo in a manner which inspires others to welcome change rather than create tension, leading with influence rather than authority.
Act as a culture carrier who challenges the status quo constructively. Inspire cross-functional teams outside of direct reporting lines to embrace change, collaborate transparently, and break down legacy departmental silos.
Serve as a trusted adviser to provide support and strategic guidance, or take on time critical tasks with minimal prep time.
Enhance employee engagement and culture by fostering a positive work environment, promoting employee development, and recognizing and rewarding employee contributions.

Must Have(s)

Experience: Minimum of 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in fixed income markets, both in Canada and internationally, with a specific focus on the repo market and clearing markets, alongside a proven track record of delivering enterprise-scale market infrastructure programs.
Market Knowledge: Deep expertise in the Canadian fixed income and repo markets, combined with strong analytical skills to inform and execute strategic direction.
Product Expertise: Proven experience working on complex fixed income products and market structures, including repo clearing.
Commercial Engagement: Demonstrated commercial success and hands-on experience in engaging with buy-side and sell-side firms across Canadian and US markets to address complex operational and regulatory needs.
People Leadership: Exceptional track record of managing and transforming complex teams, developing future leaders, and driving high employee engagement scores in a fast-paced environment.
Matrix Leadership: Proven experience leading cross-functional teams in a complex environment (solid-line/matrix reporting) where resources must balance functional standards with strict program delivery timelines.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related technical discipline.

Nice To Have(s)

Regulatory Experience: Demonstrated experience in engaging with central banks or other regulatory bodies on market initiatives is highly desirable.
Advanced Credentials: An MBA, CFA, or advanced degree in project/program management is highly desirable.
Governance Frameworks: Direct experience designing and executing formal project governance models, including RACI frameworks, cross-organizational risk management, and formal steering committee reporting is highly desirable.
Language Skills: Fluency in English and French is an asset, given regular communications with internal teams and external stakeholders.

In the market for…

Excitement
- Explore emerging technology and innovation, as well as ventures and digital finance that shape the future of global markets! Experience the movement of the market while grounded in the stability of close to 200 years of success.

Connection
- With site hubs in some of the world’s most multicultural cities, we leverage our size and structure to create rich connections and belonging while experiencing powerful global impact through our work.

Impact
- More than a platform, we use our talents to power mission-critical systems that drive global economic advancement, innovation, and growth. As well, our employee-led Team Impact spreads social good via our giving strategy.

Wellness
- From empathetic leadership to a culture of flexibility and balance, we believe wellness at work creates the maximum yield and a stronger “we”. Plus, with a cloud-first and hybrid workstyle, as well as generous time-off and leaves, we support a life well lived!

Growth
- From a growth mindset in our work, to expansion in our business, TMX is home to action-takers energized by the achievement of ambitious growth.

Ready to enrich your career with impactful work, leaders who truly care, and the flexibility and programs to help you thrive as part of #TeamTMX ? Apply now.

jobs.title: AVP Third Party Risk Management
jobs.description:
We are hiring for this position out of our Toronto, Calgary, and Vancouver offices. Successful candidates who apply outside of these areas will be expected to relocate and reside in a location that is within a commutable distance.

Role Overview

The Assistant Vice President, Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) is responsible for leading the implementation and ongoing execution of the Peoples Group TPRM framework, including ownership of the TPRM policy, supporting toolkits, inventory, and compliance tracking. This role leads and develops a team accountable for running the TPRM program, providing effective challenge to third‑party risk and criticality assessments, and ensuring regulatory requirements are met across the enterprise.

The AVP prepares regular reporting for senior management and Board committees, partners closely with Technology on the development and maintenance of the TPRM system, and works collaboratively with Legal, Procurement, Information Security, and Relationship Owners to manage third‑party onboarding, contracting, cyber risk, and ongoing monitoring. Success in this role requires strong stakeholder and conflict management skills to balance business objectives, client expectations, and regulatory obligations, as well as the ability to build productive relationships across multiple departments and drive enterprise‑wide training and compliance with TPRM requirements.

About The Day-to-day

Lead the implementation of the Peoples Group TPRM framework.
Responsible for maintaining the TPRM Policy and Framework as well as the documentation supporting TPRM toolkits (Criticality and Risk Triage, Risk Assessment Template, Due Diligence Questionnaire, Contracting Requirements, Monitoring Plans, Contingency and Exit Planning, Exception Management).
Manage a team of analysts and senior managers accountable for running the TPRM Framework. Lead the team in providing constructive challenge to the results of third-party risk and criticality assessments completed by the Relationship Owners.
Own and manage the TPRM inventory and compliance tracker.
Prepare regular reporting for the Operational Risk Management Committee, Corporate Risk Committee and Board Risk Committee.
Work directly with the Technology team on the development and launch of the TPRM system to facilitate completion of the required toolkits and inventory of required Third-Party documentation. This includes accountability for User Acceptance Testing prior to launch and for regular patches and updates from the software provider.
Successfully manage friction arising between business objectives, client expectations and regulatory requirements. Account Managers and their clients are important stakeholders in the success of TPRM. The successful candidate will be relied on to diffuse tensions when working with clients and counterparties to meet regulatory requirements for TPRM.
Develop and coordinate enterprise-wide training on TPRM requirements.
Work directly with Relationship Owners to clarify requirements for the onboarding and management of Third-Parties.
Work closely with the Legal and Procurement departments to maintain control processes and compliance requirements when onboarding new Third-Parties and executing contracts.
Coordinate with the Information Security Team to assess cyber-security control effectiveness at critical third parties.
Working across all departments within PTC, partnering with relationship owners to maintain compliance and update third-party criticality and risk assessment. Collaboratively escalating gaps with requirements and facilitating approval of waivers where appropriate.
Establishing productive relationships and working successfully with stakeholders across multiple departments is essential for success in this role.

About The Qualifications

10+ years experience working in risk management or operations at a Canadian Financial Institution, with at least 5 years of experience in a management role.
Successfully delivered enterprise-wide risk projects requiring significant change management and training across departments.
Familiarity with Software Development Life Cycle in the context of enterprise applications and experience developing requirements for risk management solutions and coordinating User Acceptance Testing.
Required experience in developing Third Party Risk Management TPRM Frameworks at Small and Medium Sized Banks (SMSBs) in Canada. Alternatively, applicants with intricate knowledge and experience in running an established TPRM framework at an SMSB or DSIB will also be considered.
Direct experience in managing OSFI expectation and regulatory findings related to TPRM and Guideline B-10 is a significant asset.
Strong communication skills, with experience presenting at senior management committee meetings and interacting directly with C-level executives at SMSBs.
Proven conflict management capabilities when working across multiple departments and stakeholders to achieve positive risk and compliance outcomes.

About Us

Peoples Group is a trusted financial services company for the innovators at the forefront of Canada’s economic future. With offices in Vancouver, Calgary, and Toronto, we are driving change by working alongside challenger banks, fintechs, brokers, and merchants to foster a dynamic and competitive financial ecosystem.

Our culture is built on four core behaviours: Grit to Grow
, Connect to Collaborate
, Putting Clients First
, and Owning the Outcome
. We believe people do not simply choose a company to work for—they choose a company that makes a positive impact in the lives of Canadians. Above all, we value people, build meaningful relationships, focus on individual strengths, and approach our work with passion.

About The Work Environment

Peoples Group offers a flexible and hybrid work environment. In this role you will work a combination of in-office and remotely from home. Typically, you'll be working regular business hours, Monday to Friday between 8:00am and 4:30pm with flexibility around start/end times.

We Offer

A hybrid work environment, enabling you to balance your personal and professional life seamlessly.
Competitive salaries, profit sharing, RRSP matching and benefits from day one.
Generous paid time off to help achieve a healthy work-life balance.
A strengths-based approach, ensuring we work together more effectively.
A commitment to your well-being in five key areas: Financial, Physical, Social, Career, and Community.

Peoples Group is pleased to offer employees a competitive annual salary plus a discretionary profit share opportunity. Salary for this position will vary between $130,000 and $145,000 per year depending on the knowledge, skills, abilities and experience that the chosen candidate possesses.

The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets. United as a global team, we’re connecting cross-functionally, traversing industries and geographies, moving opportunity into action, advancing global economic growth, and propelling progress. Through a rich exchange of ideas, meaningful collaboration, and a nimble operating model, we're powering some of the nation's most critical systems, fueling capital formation and innovation, bringing increased opportunity to business visionaries, product ingenuity to consumers, and career exploration to our team.

Ready to be part of the action?

Reporting to the President, CDCC, this role is a critical strategic resource focused on accelerating Post Trade's strategy and objectives. The Managing Director will drive the execution of complex, high-impact market modernization initiatives, providing dedicated delivery leadership to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC.

The main function of this role is to provide dedicated support to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC in delivering the Post Trade product and client centric solutions. Success hinges on a proven capital markets expert with deep knowledge of the Canadian capital markets, with an emphasis on fixed income, derivatives and repo markets knowledge, established relationships with key industry stakeholders. This expertise is vital in driving strategic development and managing complex alignment across TMX and core industry partners, including the Bank of Canada (BoC) and CIMPA participants, optimizing and aligning the Post Trade delivery strategy, with special initial focus on delivering and establishing the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and Repo 2.0.

Reports To: President, CDCC and Co-Head, Post-Trade Services
Job Location: This role is hybrid (2-3 days/week in the office) - we are open to candidates being located in one of our Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal.

Key Responsibilities

Program Delivery, Stakeholder Coordination, and Optimization
Unified Product-to-Delivery Lifecycle: Partner deeply with the Product Teams across Post Trade to translate product visions, commercial goals, and market requirements into robust, executable program delivery roadmaps.
Cross-Functional Delivery Governance: Establish rigorous execution frameworks, milestones, and governance models that ensure Post-Trade Innovations, CDCC, and CDS operate in perfect lockstep.
Strategy and Delivery Support: Provide dedicated, strategic and delivery support to Post Trade Innovations, CDCC and CDS to ensure the efficient execution of the overarching Post Trade delivery strategy.
Strategic Initiative Leadership: Provide strategic support for the execution and alignment of major market modernization initiatives, specifically the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and the Repo program.
Central Bank Coordination: Serve as the primary liaison to ensure strategic and operational alignment required for the Bank of Canada's (BoC) integration into the Post Trade framework, including the implementation of the CCP tri-party repo platform.
Market and Client Engagement: Help cultivate and maintain relationships with key stakeholders (e.g., BoC, CIMPA) to gather strategic insights, champion clearing initiatives, and validate new service proposals for Post Trade.
Internal Alignment: Ensure optimal, formalized deliveries with key internal stakeholders to efficiently advance CCMS, Repo 2.0, and other core business objectives.

Governance & Execution Frameworks
Enforce key governance, including the formal escalation path and milestone criteria.
Take direct responsibility for strategic and operational conflict resolution across CDS and CDCC business lines.

Execution & Representation

Establish a strict pre-briefing protocol for client engagements to ensure unified messaging regarding value propositions.
Design and implement a mandatory, structured knowledge-transfer and cross-training program to decentralize business and product expertise.

Implement unified resource-tracking dashboards for visibility into team capacity and competing priorities.
Provide formal performance evaluation input to the functional leaders of dedicated resources.
Maintain authority to initiate external recruiting processes if internal resource constraints delay critical strategic deliverables.

Manage hiring, training and development of team members; set comprehensive objectives for individual and organizational performance and growth, enforcing accountability at all levels.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related technical discipline.

new_jobs.description:
We are hiring for this position out of our Toronto, Calgary, and Vancouver offices. Successful candidates who apply outside of these areas will be expected to relocate and reside in a location that is within a commutable distance.

Role Overview

The Assistant Vice President, Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) is responsible for leading the implementation and ongoing execution of the Peoples Group TPRM framework, including ownership of the TPRM policy, supporting toolkits, inventory, and compliance tracking. This role leads and develops a team accountable for running the TPRM program, providing effective challenge to third‑party risk and criticality assessments, and ensuring regulatory requirements are met across the enterprise.

The AVP prepares regular reporting for senior management and Board committees, partners closely with Technology on the development and maintenance of the TPRM system, and works collaboratively with Legal, Procurement, Information Security, and Relationship Owners to manage third‑party onboarding, contracting, cyber risk, and ongoing monitoring. Success in this role requires strong stakeholder and conflict management skills to balance business objectives, client expectations, and regulatory obligations, as well as the ability to build productive relationships across multiple departments and drive enterprise‑wide training and compliance with TPRM requirements.

About The Day-to-day

Lead the implementation of the Peoples Group TPRM framework.
Responsible for maintaining the TPRM Policy and Framework as well as the documentation supporting TPRM toolkits (Criticality and Risk Triage, Risk Assessment Template, Due Diligence Questionnaire, Contracting Requirements, Monitoring Plans, Contingency and Exit Planning, Exception Management).
Manage a team of analysts and senior managers accountable for running the TPRM Framework. Lead the team in providing constructive challenge to the results of third-party risk and criticality assessments completed by the Relationship Owners.
Own and manage the TPRM inventory and compliance tracker.
Prepare regular reporting for the Operational Risk Management Committee, Corporate Risk Committee and Board Risk Committee.
Work directly with the Technology team on the development and launch of the TPRM system to facilitate completion of the required toolkits and inventory of required Third-Party documentation. This includes accountability for User Acceptance Testing prior to launch and for regular patches and updates from the software provider.
Successfully manage friction arising between business objectives, client expectations and regulatory requirements. Account Managers and their clients are important stakeholders in the success of TPRM. The successful candidate will be relied on to diffuse tensions when working with clients and counterparties to meet regulatory requirements for TPRM.
Develop and coordinate enterprise-wide training on TPRM requirements.
Work directly with Relationship Owners to clarify requirements for the onboarding and management of Third-Parties.
Work closely with the Legal and Procurement departments to maintain control processes and compliance requirements when onboarding new Third-Parties and executing contracts.
Coordinate with the Information Security Team to assess cyber-security control effectiveness at critical third parties.
Working across all departments within PTC, partnering with relationship owners to maintain compliance and update third-party criticality and risk assessment. Collaboratively escalating gaps with requirements and facilitating approval of waivers where appropriate.
Establishing productive relationships and working successfully with stakeholders across multiple departments is essential for success in this role.

About The Qualifications

10+ years experience working in risk management or operations at a Canadian Financial Institution, with at least 5 years of experience in a management role.
Successfully delivered enterprise-wide risk projects requiring significant change management and training across departments.
Familiarity with Software Development Life Cycle in the context of enterprise applications and experience developing requirements for risk management solutions and coordinating User Acceptance Testing.
Required experience in developing Third Party Risk Management TPRM Frameworks at Small and Medium Sized Banks (SMSBs) in Canada. Alternatively, applicants with intricate knowledge and experience in running an established TPRM framework at an SMSB or DSIB will also be considered.
Direct experience in managing OSFI expectation and regulatory findings related to TPRM and Guideline B-10 is a significant asset.
Strong communication skills, with experience presenting at senior management committee meetings and interacting directly with C-level executives at SMSBs.
Proven conflict management capabilities when working across multiple departments and stakeholders to achieve positive risk and compliance outcomes.

About Us

Peoples Group is a trusted financial services company for the innovators at the forefront of Canada’s economic future. With offices in Vancouver, Calgary, and Toronto, we are driving change by working alongside challenger banks, fintechs, brokers, and merchants to foster a dynamic and competitive financial ecosystem.

Our culture is built on four core behaviours: Grit to Grow
, Connect to Collaborate
, Putting Clients First
, and Owning the Outcome
. We believe people do not simply choose a company to work for—they choose a company that makes a positive impact in the lives of Canadians. Above all, we value people, build meaningful relationships, focus on individual strengths, and approach our work with passion.

About The Work Environment

Peoples Group offers a flexible and hybrid work environment. In this role you will work a combination of in-office and remotely from home. Typically, you'll be working regular business hours, Monday to Friday between 8:00am and 4:30pm with flexibility around start/end times.

We Offer

A hybrid work environment, enabling you to balance your personal and professional life seamlessly.
Competitive salaries, profit sharing, RRSP matching and benefits from day one.
Generous paid time off to help achieve a healthy work-life balance.
A strengths-based approach, ensuring we work together more effectively.
A commitment to your well-being in five key areas: Financial, Physical, Social, Career, and Community.

Peoples Group is pleased to offer employees a competitive annual salary plus a discretionary profit share opportunity. Salary for this position will vary between $130,000 and $145,000 per year depending on the knowledge, skills, abilities and experience that the chosen candidate possesses.

This role is a member of the Retirement and Wealth Marketing leadership team and reports directly to the Head of Retirement and Wealth Marketing.

Position Responsibilities

Marketing Strategy and Planning

Lead the development and alignment of annual and in-year marketing plans.
Translate enterprise and business priorities into clear marketing objectives and investment choices.
Coordinate dependencies, trade-offs, and changes across portfolios and initiatives.

Business Management and Operating Rhythm

Establish planning, governance, reporting, and decision-making forums.
Prepare decision-ready materials and ensure timely follow-through on commitments.
Identify and escalate delivery risks, resource constraints, and cross-functional dependencies.
Define and monitor marketing KPIs and campaign effectiveness across regions, including monthly business reporting to global marketing and quarterly reporting on key KPIs and accomplishments.
Use AI, insights and analytics to support planning and executive reporting, evaluate activities, and identify opportunities for shared approaches and efficiencies across regions.
Surface data limitations and opportunities to improve measurement.

Budget Management and Financial Oversight

Lead annual budget planning for Retirement and Wealth Marketing, working with marketing leaders and Finance to align funding with business priorities and planned initiatives.
Manage ongoing budget tracking and forecasting, providing a consolidated view of spending, commitments, and anticipated expenses.
Coordinate monthly budget and expense reviews with Finance and marketing leaders; assess actual versus planned spending and cost pressures, and recommend forecast, spending and resource adjustments to support priorities within approved budgets.
Prepare financial reporting for leadership that explains budget performance, risks, trade-offs, and decisions required.
Partner with Finance and Procurement on financial assumptions, vendor and marketing technology selection, commitments, and required approvals.
Serve as the central contact for strategic funding requests, supporting business cases that define requirements, costs, expected outcomes, and KPIs to track success.

The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets. Ready to be part of the action?

Reporting to the President, CDCC, this role is a critical strategic resource focused on accelerating Post Trade's strategy and objectives. The Managing Director will drive the execution of complex, high-impact market modernization initiatives, providing dedicated delivery leadership to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC.

The main function of this role is to provide dedicated support to Post-Trade Innovations and CDCC in delivering the Post Trade product and client centric solutions. Success hinges on a proven capital markets expert with deep knowledge of the Canadian capital markets, with an emphasis on fixed income, derivatives and repo markets knowledge, established relationships with key industry stakeholders. This expertise is vital in driving strategic development and managing complex alignment across TMX and core industry partners, including the Bank of Canada (BoC) and CIMPA participants, optimizing and aligning the Post Trade delivery strategy, with special initial focus on delivering and establishing the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and Repo 2.0.

Reports To: President, CDCC and Co-Head, Post-Trade Services
Job Location: This role is hybrid (2-3 days/week in the office) - we are open to candidates being located in one of our Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal.

Key Responsibilities

Program Delivery, Stakeholder Coordination, and Optimization
Unified Product-to-Delivery Lifecycle: Partner deeply with the Product Teams across Post Trade to translate product visions, commercial goals, and market requirements into robust, executable program delivery roadmaps.
Cross-Functional Delivery Governance: Establish rigorous execution frameworks, milestones, and governance models that ensure Post-Trade Innovations, CDCC, and CDS operate in perfect lockstep.
Strategy and Delivery Support: Provide dedicated, strategic and delivery support to Post Trade Innovations, CDCC and CDS to ensure the efficient execution of the overarching Post Trade delivery strategy.
Strategic Initiative Leadership: Provide strategic support for the execution and alignment of major market modernization initiatives, specifically the Canadian Collateral Management Service (CCMS) and the Repo program.
Central Bank Coordination: Serve as the primary liaison to ensure strategic and operational alignment required for the Bank of Canada's (BoC) integration into the Post Trade framework, including the implementation of the CCP tri-party repo platform.
Market and Client Engagement: Help cultivate and maintain relationships with key stakeholders (e.g., BoC, CIMPA) to gather strategic insights, champion clearing initiatives, and validate new service proposals for Post Trade.
Internal Alignment: Ensure optimal, formalized deliveries with key internal stakeholders to efficiently advance CCMS, Repo 2.0, and other core business objectives.

Enforce key governance, including the formal escalation path and milestone criteria.
Take direct responsibility for strategic and operational conflict resolution across CDS and CDCC business lines.

Execution & Representation

Establish a strict pre-briefing protocol for client engagements to ensure unified messaging regarding value propositions.
Design and implement a mandatory, structured knowledge-transfer and cross-training program to decentralize business and product expertise.

Enforce mandatory participation of all dedicated resources in CCMS squad meetings and planning sessions.
Implement unified resource-tracking dashboards for visibility into team capacity and competing priorities.
Provide formal performance evaluation input to the functional leaders of dedicated resources.
Maintain authority to initiate external recruiting processes if internal resource constraints delay critical strategic deliverables.

Leadership and Guidance
Manage hiring, training and development of team members; set comprehensive objectives for individual and organizational performance and growth, enforcing accountability at all levels.
Recruit, mentor, and elevate a world-class team of delivery professionals and subject matter experts. Instill a culture of extreme ownership, high psychological safety, and continuous improvement.
Collaborate with other senior resources to ensure that objectives are aligned across all functions and business units, and create a culture of change and continuous improvement.
Challenge the status quo in a manner which inspires others to welcome change rather than create tension, leading with influence rather than authority.
Act as a culture carrier who challenges the status quo constructively. Inspire cross-functional teams outside of direct reporting lines to embrace change, collaborate transparently, and break down legacy departmental silos.
Serve as a trusted adviser to provide support and strategic guidance, or take on time critical tasks with minimal prep time.
Enhance employee engagement and culture by fostering a positive work environment, promoting employee development, and recognizing and rewarding employee contributions.

Experience: Minimum of 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in fixed income markets, both in Canada and internationally, with a specific focus on the repo market and clearing markets, alongside a proven track record of delivering enterprise-scale market infrastructure programs.
Market Knowledge: Deep expertise in the Canadian fixed income and repo markets, combined with strong analytical skills to inform and execute strategic direction.
Product Expertise: Proven experience working on complex fixed income products and market structures, including repo clearing.
Commercial Engagement: Demonstrated commercial success and hands-on experience in engaging with buy-side and sell-side firms across Canadian and US markets to address complex operational and regulatory needs.
People Leadership: Exceptional track record of managing and transforming complex teams, developing future leaders, and driving high employee engagement scores in a fast-paced environment.
Matrix Leadership: Proven experience leading cross-functional teams in a complex environment (solid-line/matrix reporting) where resources must balance functional standards with strict program delivery timelines.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related technical discipline.

Regulatory Experience: Demonstrated experience in engaging with central banks or other regulatory bodies on market initiatives is highly desirable.
Advanced Credentials: An MBA, CFA, or advanced degree in project/program management is highly desirable.
Governance Frameworks: Direct experience designing and executing formal project governance models, including RACI frameworks, cross-organizational risk management, and formal steering committee reporting is highly desirable.
Language Skills: Fluency in English and French is an asset, given regular communications with internal teams and external stakeholders.

- Explore emerging technology and innovation, as well as ventures and digital finance that shape the future of global markets! Experience the movement of the market while grounded in the stability of close to 200 years of success.

Connection

Impact

Growth
